comment: Lexical tier of the remove-ai-slop catalog: everything regex can catch. Structural patterns (triads, paragraph shape, rhythm, section symmetry) live in references/patterns.md and are measured by scan.mjs's structural tier. Nothing here is a finding — every hit is a candidate the close-reading pass must judge in context. Categories: vocabulary | phrase | construction | punctuation | chatbot | artifact.

patterns.name: AI vocabulary: crucial/pivotal/vital/paramount
patterns.note: Fine occasionally; a tell when recurring.

patterns.name: AI vocabulary: delve/plethora/myriad
patterns.note: The canonical 2023-2024 cluster. Ordinary in Indian and West-African English — check the document's register before flagging.

patterns.name: AI vocabulary: landscape/realm/ever-evolving (abstract)
patterns.note: Suspicious as an abstract noun ('the AI landscape'), fine literally.

patterns.name: Grandeur metaphors: tapestry/beacon/cornerstone/catalyst
patterns.note: Borrowed-grandeur cluster; judge figurative use only.

patterns.name: Significance inflation: testament/underscore/pivotal moment
patterns.regex: \b(testament to|underscor(e|es|ed|ing)|highlight(s|ed|ing)? (the )?(importance|significance)|pivotal (moment|role)|turning point|indelible mark|setting the stage for|deeply rooted|reflects broader|solidif(y|ies|ied|ying) (its|their|his|her) position)\b
patterns.note: State the fact and let the reader judge whether it matters.

patterns.name: Inflation verbs: leverage/harness/unlock/empower/foster
patterns.note: Suspicious in figurative use. Check for domain-literal uses first ('harness' as a noun in agent engineering, 'leverage' in finance).

patterns.name: Promotional: seamless/robust/groundbreaking/cutting-edge
patterns.note: Legitimate in marketing copy; a tell in neutral or technical registers.

patterns.name: AI vocabulary: intricate/meticulous/nuanced/multifaceted
patterns.note: 'complex and multifaceted' is reported ~700x more common in AI text.

patterns.name: Assistant soft signals: honest/genuinely/truly/simply
patterns.note: Empty intensifiers in an assistant's default register. Keep when they carry real emphasis, uncertainty, or contrast; a tell when recurring.

patterns.name: Conjunctive openers: Additionally/Moreover/Furthermore/Notably
patterns.note: Individually normal; a tell at density.

patterns.name: Hedge transitions: That said / generally speaking / typically
patterns.regex: \b(That (being )?said,|Generally speaking|in most cases|in many cases|while this may vary|more often than not)\b
patterns.note: Watch for hedge stacks: three qualifiers before any claim.

patterns.name: Signposting: let's take a closer look / each in turn
patterns.regex: \b(let('|’)s (take a closer look|look at each|dive|unpack|walk through|explore|examine|break (this|it) down)|each in turn|in turn\.|take a closer look|without further ado|in this (article|post|section|chapter), (we|I)('|’)ll)\b
patterns.note: Legitimate in reference documentation, where announcing structure is the job. A tell in essays, posts, and narrative prose.

patterns.name: Throat-clearing opener: here's the thing / let me be clear
patterns.regex: \b(here(('|’)s| is) (the thing|what I mean|the deal|why)|let me be clear|I('|’)ll be honest|to be honest|the (uncomfortable|hard|simple|inconvenient) truth is|the reality is|the truth is)\b
patterns.note: Cut the frame and state the point. Keep only when the aside is genuinely personal.

patterns.name: Faux-insight setup: what nobody tells you / most people miss
patterns.regex: \b(what (nobody|no one) tells you|(most|what most) people (get wrong|miss|skip|don('|’)t (realize|know))|the part (everyone|most people) miss(es)?|this is the part (most people|everyone) skips|here('|’)s what (nobody|most people))\b
patterns.note: Flatters the writer as the lone expert. Cut the setup; let the claim stand alone.

patterns.name: Filler frames: at its core / the key insight / put simply
patterns.regex: \b(at its (core|heart)|at the heart of|the key (insight|takeaway|point)|put simply|simply put|in essence|when it comes to|in terms of|with regard to|going forward|at the end of the day|here('|’)s the key)\b

patterns.name: Cliché: plays a X role in / deeper understanding / valuable insights
patterns.regex: \b(play(s|ed|ing)? an? \w+ role in|a deeper understanding of|(valuable|actionable|key) insights|in today('|’)s (fast-paced|digital|rapidly|world)|in the (age|world) of)\b
patterns.note: 'play a significant role in shaping' measured 182x more frequent in AI text.

patterns.name: Vague attribution: experts argue / studies show
patterns.note: Name the source or cut the claim. Never invent a citation to satisfy this.

patterns.name: Formulaic conclusion: in conclusion / the future looks bright
patterns.regex: \b(in conclusion|in summary|to sum(marize| up)|the future (looks|is) (bright|promising)|exciting times|one thing is (clear|certain)|only time will tell|despite these challenges)\b
patterns.note: Recaps that restate rather than add. End on the last concrete point instead.

patterns.name: "Not X but Y" contrast
patterns.regex: \b(not (just|merely|only|simply|about)\b|isn('|’)t (just|merely|only|simply|about)\b|doesn('|’)t just\b|has nothing to do with|the (question|issue|point|problem) isn('|’)t|less about \w+[^.]{0,40} and more about|not with \w+[^.]{0,40}, but with)
patterns.note: Negation-then-redefinition: the most-cited syntactic tell, and the one reviewers quote back. State Y directly.

patterns.name: Full-rejection contrast: It is not X. It is Y.
patterns.note: The bare form of §1.1: reject, then redefine in the next sentence. Check that the second sentence really restates the first — 'It is not ready. It is broken.' is ordinary English.

patterns.name: Negative listing: Not a X. Not a Y.
patterns.note: Staccato stack of rejections before the real claim. Just state the claim.

patterns.name: Colon reveal: noun-phrase fragment, colon, dramatic clause
patterns.note: 'The best part: it learns.' Manufactured drama — the pre-colon span is a verbless fragment. Verify that before flagging: a colon introducing a genuine list, definition, or example is correct. Rewrite as a plain sentence with a verb.

patterns.name: Rhetorical setup: what if I told you / plot twist / the result?
patterns.regex: \b(what if I told you|think about it|plot twist|here('|’)s the (kicker|twist)|the (result|catch|problem|answer|kicker)\?|sound familiar\?|have you ever wondered)
patterns.note: Self-answered question used as a pivot. Drop it and make the point.

patterns.name: Preference framing: X rather than Y / instead of
patterns.note: §1.13. Weak on its own and often correct — judge at density, never one instance. Its real importance is as the landing site for a laundered §1.1: a fix pass that removes 'not X but Y' and re-lands the same contrast here has moved the tell, not removed it (§9.2). On a re-scan, if this rose while the negation patterns fell, that is the substitution, not progress.

patterns.name: Semicolon hedge pair (reduce; not eliminate)
patterns.note: Balanced concede-and-retain. One is fine; recurring, it is a metronome.

patterns.name: Copula avoidance: serves as/stands as/boasts
patterns.note: Prefer 'is' and 'has' when they are clearer.

patterns.name: Nominalized verb: made a decision / has the ability to
patterns.regex: \b(mak(e|es|ing)|made|tak(e|es|ing)|took|provid(e|es|ing)|conduct(s|ed|ing)?|perform(s|ed|ing)?) an? (decision|assessment|determination|comparison|contribution|improvement|reduction|solution|analysis|evaluation)\b|\b(has|have|had) the ability to\b|\bin order to\b|\bis able to\b
patterns.note: 'made a decision' → 'decided'. 'has the ability to' → 'can'. Let verbs do the work.

patterns.name: Trailing -ing analysis (highlighting/ensuring/reflecting…)
patterns.note: Present-participle clause tacked on for fake depth. Replace with the concrete consequence, or cut.

patterns.name: False range: from X to Y (no real scale)
patterns.note: Only slop when X and Y sit on no meaningful scale — test whether you could name something between them.

patterns.name: Aphoristic contrast: the difference between X and Y
patterns.note: A tell when used as a paragraph-closing aphorism, not when it introduces a real distinction.

patterns.name: Em dash
patterns.note: Judge by density (>3/1k words) and by additive use — bolting on a qualifier rather than interrupting. Measured 5.4/1k in Claude output vs 1.1/1k in GPT.

patterns.name: Chatbot artifact (I hope this helps / Certainly!)
patterns.regex: \b(I hope this (helps|message|email)|Certainly!|Of course!|Absolutely!|You('|’)re absolutely right|Great question|That('|’)s a (great|brilliant) (question|observation)|let me know if|Would you like me to|Feel free to ask|As an AI language model|as of my last (knowledge|training) update)\b
patterns.note: Near-proof. Always HIGH, even once.

patterns.name: Machine citation marker / unfilled placeholder
patterns.note: Near-proof of machine generation or an unfinished paste. Always HIGH.
